Fume extractor

Layers, front to back

How it holds together

  • One set of screws: , all from the front of L5, through L4 and L3 into . Four pass through the fan's own corner holes; two hold the chin. The back shows no screws.
  • Face: no screws. A 3 mm lip drops into the pad pocket, and magnets hold it on (). The 4 fan screws sit 2 mm deep in L5, and a magnet clings to each steel head (use zinc-plated steel screws, not stainless). The face's magnets snap onto them.
  • Filters: front: pull the face off. Rear: pull the face off, pick out the 4 magnets, undo the 6 screws, and the stack lifts off the back part.
  • Handle: 2 × M4 heat-set inserts in the top, 50.8 mm apart, which matches the end holes of a 5-hole Meccano strip. Fit two M4 standoffs and screw the strip on top.
  • Pads: cut each one 80 mm square and snip 16 mm off every corner, which clears the screws.
  • Wiring: the fan lead drops into the hollow chin through a notch in L3, then runs to the jack and switch on L4's right side.

Measure before printing

  • M4 heat-set insert: outside diameter and lengthØ5.7 bore × 7 assumed
  • Carbon pad: thickness10 assumed
  • Fan: is it 12 V or 24 V? The adaptor tops out at 12 V.
  • DC jack: panel hole sizeØ8 assumed
  • Switch: type and hole sizeØ6 toggle assumed
  • M3 heat-set insert length≤ 6 assumed
  • Can you buy M3 × 60 countersunk? If not, M3 × 60 socket head fits the same seats.
